extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (those preparing or examining U.S. patent application filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for the form, content, electronic/media formats, and procedural submission requirements of U.S. patent applications (including read-only optical discs, large tables, sequence listings, translations, drawings, and prohibited content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted read-only optical disc document types
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents may be submitted on a read-only optical disc in compliance with paragraph (e): (i) A 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' (§ 1.96(c)); (ii) A 'Sequence Listing' (submitted under § 1.821(c) in compliance with §§ 1.822–1.824) or a 'Sequence Listing XML' (submitted under § 1.831(a) in compliance with §§ 1.832–1.834); or (iii) 'Large Tables' (see § 1.58(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read-only optical disc submissions are limited to these document types; other materials should be submitted by applicable electronic filing methods or as part of the application papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc physical and filesystem requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'read-only optical disc' must be finalized, conform to ISO 9660, be permanent (data cannot be changed or erased), and be one of: Compact Disc-Read-Only Memory (CD–ROM) or Compact Disc-Recordable (CD–R); or Digital Video Disc-Recordable (DVD–R or DVD+R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disc must be a finalized (non-writable) ISO 9660-conforming medium so Office can archive it permanently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc computer/OS and file format compatibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must be compatible with PC or Mac and operating systems MS–DOS, MS–Windows, MacOS, or Unix/Linux. Contents must be ASCII plain text (if compressed, compressed per the applicable section) or, for Sequence Listing XML, XML file format (and if compressed must follow § 1.834).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow referenced compression and format rules for the specific document type (Large Tables §1.58, Computer Program Listing §1.96, Sequence Listing §1.824/1.834).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter information for read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must be accompanied by a transmittal letter including: (i) First-named inventor; (ii) Title of the invention; (iii) Attorney docket/file reference number (if applicable); (iv) Application number and filing date (if known); (v) Operating system used to produce the disc; and (vi) The file(s) on the disc (file name, size in bytes, date of creation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal letter must conform to paragraph (a) requirements and enable prompt association and processing of the disc contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirements for read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disc must have a permanent label (hand-printed or typed) with: (i) First-named inventor; (ii) Title of the invention; (iii) Attorney docket/file reference (if applicable); (iv) Application number and filing date (if known); (v) Date data were recorded on the disc; (vi) Disc order (e.g., '1 of X') if multiple discs submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels must be permanently affixed and clearly identify disc contents and order to avoid processing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical discs are not returned/retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Read-only optical discs will not be returned to the applicant and may not be retained as part of the patent application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should keep their own copies; do not expect original discs to remain with the file or to be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of information on read-only optical discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to information on a read-only optical disc must be by way of a replacement read-only optical disc, complying with the specific replacement provisions referenced for Large Tables (§ 1.58(g)), Computer Program Listing Appendix (§ 1.96(c)(5)), Sequence Listing (§ 1.825(b)), or Sequence Listing XML (§ 1.835(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt in-place edits; submit a properly labeled replacement disc as required by the applicable section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreadable electronic files treated as not submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file on a read-only optical disc is unreadable, it will be treated as not having been submitted, and a notice will be issued to require a compliant submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure files are readable on supported systems; unreadable files cause non-submission status and require corrective action within a time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee calculation for read-only optical disc content
rubrics_metrics.description: For components submitted in part on a read-only optical disc, each three kilobytes of content submitted on the disc shall be counted as a sheet of paper for application size fee determination, excluding ASCII plain text files or XML files for Sequence Listings, Sequence Listing CRFs, or Computer Program Listing Appendix as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings and program listing appendices submitted on discs are excluded from the 3KB-to-sheet calculation per the listed exceptions; see referenced fee regulations (§ 1.16(s), § 1.492(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee calculation for USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications submitted in whole or in part via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, the paper size equivalent will be considered to be 75% of the number of sheets of paper present in the specification and drawings when entered into Office records after rendering by the system. Excluded are ASCII plain text files or XML files containing Sequence Listings or Computer Program Listing Appendices in compliance with the cited sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS rendering reduces counted paper-equivalent size to 75%; sequence listings/program listings excluded from this calculation when compliant with their sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversized sequence listing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission of a Sequence Listing in electronic form or a Sequence Listing XML of 300 MB–800 MB filed in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 or 371 will be subject to the fee set forth in § 1.21(o)(1). Any submission that exceeds 800 MB will be subject to the fee in § 1.21(o)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large sequence listing file sizes trigger specific oversized-file fees; monitor file sizes before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and mathematical formulas/tables allowed but no drawings/flow diagrams in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, including the claims, may contain chemical and mathematical formulae, but shall not contain drawings or flow diagrams. The description may contain tables, but the same tables should not be included in both the drawings and the description portion of the specification. Claims may contain tables if necessary to conform to 35 U.S.C. 112 or otherwise desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If descriptive illustrations such as graphs or flowcharts appear in the descriptive portion, examiners should object and request drawings under 37 CFR 1.81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation standards for chemical/mathematical formulas and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulas and tables must comply with § 1.52(a) and (b); may be placed landscape if necessary; typewritten characters must be from a block (nonscript) font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier) with capital letters preferably 0.422 cm (0.166 in) high (e.g., 12 pt), but no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 in) (e.g., 6 pt). Provide at least 0.64 cm (0.25 in) space between complex formulas/tables and text. Chemical/mathematical formulas must preserve the positioning of characters. Tables should have lines/columns closely spaced consistent with legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the minimum font sizes and spacing to ensure legibility and accurate OCR/scanning; maintain relative character positioning in formulas to preserve meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Tables eligibility for electronic ASCII submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables may be submitted in electronic ASCII plain text if: (1) any individual table is more than 50 pages in length; or (2) multiple tables total more than 100 pages (a table page is a printed page in conformance with paragraph (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thresholds govern when ASCII electronic submission of tables is permitted instead of paper tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Tables electronic ASCII file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted as ASCII plain text must: maintain spatial relationships (alignment of columns/rows); be computer-compatible (PC or Mac) and OS-compatible (MS–DOS, MS–Windows, Mac OS, Unix/Linux); be pure ASCII printable characters only (no nonprintable control characters except CRLF or LF); be named as *.txt with file name ≤ 60 characters (letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores only; no spaces); and be incorporated by reference in a separate paragraph of the specification per § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict ASCII formatting and file naming are required to preserve tabular relationships and allow Office processing; include the incorporation-by-reference paragraph in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size and compression rules for Large Tables via EFS or read-only disc
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system must not exceed 25 MB and file compression is not permitted. Large Tables submitted via read-only optical disc may be compressed using WinZip, 7-Zip, or Unix/Linux Zip, but compressed files must not be self-extracting; compressed ASCII plain text files that do not fit on a single disc may be split into multiple parts per disc size limits and labeled accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use EFS for files ≤25 MB (no compression). For larger tables, use read-only discs with allowed compressors and follow split-file labeling rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for Large Tables in electronic ASCII format
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must include: (1) a replacement ASCII plain text file complying with requirements, labeled 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'; (2) a request that the amendment be made by incorporation by reference of material in the replacement file in a separate paragraph of the specification identifying the file name, date, and size in bytes; (3) a statement identifying locations of deletions/replacements/additions to the ASCII file; (4) a statement that the replacement contains no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact labeling and specification incorporation steps, and explicitly state that replacement files introduce no new matter to avoid substantive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to incorporate Large Tables by reference in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a specification has Large Tables present as an ASCII text file on the application filing date without an incorporation-by-reference paragraph, the specification must be amended to include such a separate paragraph in accordance with § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the incorporation-by-reference paragraph for externally submitted Large Tables to meet formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate read-only optical disc submission for Large Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Any read-only optical disc for Large Tables must be submitted in duplicate labeled 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2'. The transmittal letter must state the two discs are identical; if they are not identical, the Office will use the disc labeled 'Copy 1' for processing. Replacement discs must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact duplicate discs and labeling to avoid processing ambiguity; Office will default to Copy 1 if differences exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering, line spacing, and font size/character requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages of the specification including claims and abstract must be numbered consecutively starting with 1, numbers centrally located above or preferably below the text. Lines of the specification and any amendments must be 1 1/2 or double spaced. Text must be in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier), preferably 12 pt, with capital letters at least 0.3175 cm (0.125 in) high but no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 in); text may not be written solely in capital letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formatting conventions ensure legibility and consistent reproduction; follow them to avoid objections and needs for substitute papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-sided pages and separate sheets for application parts
rubrics_metrics.description: All application papers must be plainly written on only one side of a sheet. The specification must commence on a separate sheet; each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application. Claims, abstract, and Sequence Listing (if on paper or as PDF image) should not be included on a sheet with other parts; claims must commence on separate sheet or electronic page and not contain other parts; abstract must commence on a separate sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep each application component on separate sheets/pages to conform with 37 CFR requirements and enable proper processing and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size, margins, and physical paper quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers submitted on paper must be the same size (all sheets except drawings) and be either A4 (21.0 x 29.7 cm) or US letter (21.6 x 27.9 cm). Each non-drawing sheet must have top margin ≥2.0 cm (3/4 in), left margin ≥2.5 cm (1 in), right margin ≥2.0 cm, bottom margin ≥2.0 cm. No holes should be made in sheets. Papers must be on flexible, strong, smooth, nonshiny, durable, white paper with permanent dark ink or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent sheet size and margins are required; avoid shiny or coated papers and holes that interfere with scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing system formatting and transmission compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers submitted electronically must be formatted and transmitted in compliance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements (see 37 CFR 1.52(a)(5) and MPEP § 502.05 and the Legal Framework for System Patent Electronic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EFS-specific technical and formatting rules; check MPEP §502.05 and the Legal Framework guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility and reproducibility requirement; substitute papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must file papers in a form that is clear and reproducible. If papers are not of required quality, substitute papers of suitable quality will be required per 37 CFR 1.125; all papers to become part of permanent records must be legibly written by typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink or equivalent. Gray lines/background reduce reproduction quality and may trigger a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-contrast black text on white background to maximize OCR and scanning quality; be prepared to file substitute papers if scanning/legibility issues occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to File Corrected Application Papers for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: When application papers do not comply with 37 CFR 1.52 the Office will mail a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' indicating the deficiency and setting a time period to correct it to avoid abandonment. Failure to submit compliant papers does not affect grant of a filing date; original noncompliant papers will be retained in the file as original disclosure. USPTO will not return papers simply because they do not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond timely to Notices to avoid abandonment; understand that original noncompliant papers remain part of the file and filing date stands even if papers need correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility definition and examiner evaluation phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Legibility includes ability to be photocopied and scanned so suitable reprints can be made and paper electronically reproduced by digital imaging and OCR; requires high contrast (black lines on white background). If illegible, use form paragraph identifying which parts are illegible and require a legible substitute specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should identify the specific parts that are illegible and request substitute materials per the provided examiner note guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations after oath/declaration and oath applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlineations and alterations after signing of the inventor's oath/declaration are not prohibited, but statements in the oath/declaration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.63 must remain applicable; otherwise the inventor may need to execute a new oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If post-oath changes alter the applicability of the oath statements, secure a new oath or declaration as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies of application-as-filed may be illegible if original papers noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application-as-filed does not meet sheet size/margin/quality requirements, certified copies may be illegible and/or ineffective as priority documents; the USPTO makes certified copies from IFW or microfilm databases; exception processing/ enhancement may be performed but certified copies may still be illegible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File compliant papers to ensure usable certified priority copies; do not rely on Office enhancement when original papers are poor quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute papers effect on certified copy and original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute papers filed after the application filing date will provide an image-and OCR-scannable copy for printing/publishing, but the Office treats application papers submitted after the filing date as the original disclosure for making certified copies; the USPTO will still make a copy of the application-as-filed even if substitute papers later filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing substitute papers does not change the Office's copy of the application-as-filed; certified copies reflect the as-filed record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric system recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should use the metric (S.I.) units followed by the equivalent English units when describing inventions and patent specifications to minimize future conversions when using printed patents as research and prior art search documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SI units primarily and include English equivalents for clarity; this is recommended practice (S.I. = Le Système International d'Unités).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English language application translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional application filed in a language other than English requires an English translation, a statement that the translation is accurate, and the processing fee set in § 1.17(i) (if not filed with the application the Office will notify and give time to file). Provisional applications filed in another language do not require an English translation for the provisional itself, but a translation and statement must be submitted if claiming benefit in a later nonprovisional per § 1.78(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be literal and accompanied by a statement of accuracy and a signed request to use the translation for examination. If idiomatic changes are needed, a preliminary amendment may be filed provided no new matter is introduced. Failure to timely file translation and statements will result in abandonment of the nonprovisional application or loss of the benefit claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-English filings intended for emergencies only
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application in a non-English language to secure a filing date is intended for emergency situations to prevent loss of rights and should not be routinely used because of risks of incorrect literal translations and administrative burden on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not routinely file non-English applications in lieu of filing an English application; use only for emergencies and follow translation procedures carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and graphs in the descriptive portion objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical illustrations, diagrammatic views, flowcharts, and diagrams in the descriptive portion of the specification do not come within 37 CFR 1.58(a); examiners should object to such descriptive illustrations in the specification and request drawings in accordance with 37 CFR 1.81 when the specification contains graphs, drawings, or flow charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place formal drawings in the drawings section per 1.81; do not include drawings/flow diagrams in the written description portion of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks and browser-executable code prohibition and limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other browser-executable code is not permitted (37 CFR 1.57(e)). Examiners must object to embedded hyperlinks and instruct applicants to limit website references to the top-level domain name without prefixes like 'http://'. Nucleotide/amino acid sequence data placed between '< >' are not considered hyperlinks and should not be objected to on that basis. Electronic documents listed on forms PTO-892 and PTO/SB/08 identified by URL are exempt. Hyperlinks that are themselves necessary to the invention (not the site content) and are not intended to be active links may be included but will be disabled by the Office for web display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to incorporate essential subject matter via hyperlinks; use conventional incorporation by reference or include the material in the application. If hyperlinks are embedded, use Form Paragraph 7.29.04 or 6.19/6.19.01 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner objection template for embedded hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.29.04: 'The disclosure is objected to because it contains an embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code. Applicant is required to delete the embedded hyperlink and/or other form of browser-executable code; references to websites should be limited to the top-level domain name without any prefix such as http:// or other browser-executable code.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes list examples and exceptions (sequence data between '< >', PTO-892/PTO/SB/08 documents, cases where hyperlinks themselves are part of the invention). Use this form paragraph when objecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement/order of application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet (§ 1.76); (4) Specification; (5) Drawings. Within the specification, elements such as Title, Cross-reference to related applications, Statement regarding federally sponsored research, Names of parties to joint research agreement, and incorporation-by-reference paragraphs for ASCII files/Sequence Listings/Large Tables should appear as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed order to facilitate Office processing and to ensure all required elements are present and properly placed (see 37 CFR 1.77).
